newsitem.title: USA: US Northeast spot power flat on lackluster demand.
newsitem.headline: US Northeast spot power flat on lackluster demand.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices Friday in the northeastern U.S. were little unchanged from Thursday's levels on lackluster demand due to very mild weather in the region.
"It's a depressed market with warm temperatures and no (plant) outages," a Northeast trader said. "There's no incremental sales."
The latest forecast showed temperatures in the region would run well-above normal into early next week in 40-50 Fahrenheit degree range during the day and 20-30 at night.
In the next few days, an Arctic system would hover over the most northern section of Maine, where readings would range in the single digits to the 20s.
Bulk power business in the region was light with many players still absent due to the Christmas holiday, market sources said.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices for Monday delivery in the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) held at $20.00-$22.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), although offers were heard as high as $24.00.
Off-peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in western NYPP held in a notational range of $14.00-$15.00.
In eastern NYPP, Monday's peak, non-firm power was still pegged at $26.50-$28.00/MWh.
Eastern NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Monday remained at $18.00-$19.00.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Monday at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border stayed at $30.00-$33.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for day-ahead delivery to the NU border was still assessed at $20.00-$22.00.
The temperate weather in the Northeast also dampened natural gas demand for electricity generation.
Swing prices of delivery to the New York City gate were today fell to $3.50 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu) area in line with gas futures.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, February Henry Hub natgas futures dropped as much as 42.2 cents/mmBtu to $2.960.
